Topic 10.1: Words with Mixed Accent Marks in German Braille • füré • côteä • crèmeü.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Words with Mixed Accent Marks in German Braille • füré • côteä • crèmeü., part of German Braille Notation in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use accent marks in German braille?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. explore tactile flashcards or embossed charts showing German letters with accent marks (e.g., ä, ö, ü, é, è, ß) alongside their corresponding Braille representations,

2. read prepared Braille word lists containing various accent-marked German words (schön, Mädchen, français, fuß, über, café, großmütter),

3. practice tactile reading of Braille texts containing accent marks, supported by audio pronunciation from a radio and correct each other using agreed pronunciation cues,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Words with Mixed Accent Marks in German Braille • füré • côteä • crèmeü. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Imagination and Creativity: the learner composes original Braille sentences or short texts using German words with accent

marks, demonstrating creativity in vocabulary use.

● Digital Literacy: the learner uses digital devices with assistive technology in reading and writing words with German

accent marks.

Values:
Integrity: the learner exhibits honesty in peer assessments and feedback, ensuring truthful and respectful correction of errors.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):
